newsitem.title: THAILAND: IFCT assigned to manage ailing Thai bank.
newsitem.headline: IFCT assigned to manage ailing Thai bank.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand has reached an agreement with the Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand (IFCT) to revive troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc, a central bank official said on Thursday.

He said the agreement called for IFCT to manage BBC for seven years in return for a management fee. The industrial financing bank would also share 10 percent of doubtful BBC loans that it could recall in the future.
"IFCT will have discretion to appoint a new BBC president. The name of the bank may be changed to restore its image," he said.
The central bank would have two nominees sitting on BBC's new 15-member board of directors, while IFCT would have 10 representatives on it, he said.
Other future BBC board members will come from the Thai Bankers' Association and its current shareholders.
IFCT will have an option to buy up to 51 percent of BBC equity after the third year of its management, he said.

The government took over BBC in May 1996 to save it from a massive run on its deposits. The heavy withdrawals followed charges in parliament that mismanagement by bank executives caused its non-performing loans to grow sharply.
